# Pesher Psalms Column 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Psalms Column 1 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 1:1 — Psalm 37:7 rendering — "fret not" vs. "do not be envious"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "do not fret-yourself over" | Literal Hithpael reflexive preserved with hyphen |
| LOGOS | "fret not over" | Standard English Bible rendering of *al titchar* |
| PNEUMA | "do not be envious of" | Alternate meaning of *charah* in context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "fret not over" — traditional and accurate. EMET's hyphenated reflexive is awkward; PNEUMA's "envious" shifts the semantic range.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:3 — "led astray" vs. "deceived" — characterization of the Man of the Lie

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "led-astray many with words of falsehood" | Preserves Hebrew idiom *divrei kazav* |
| LOGOS | "led many astray with deceitful words" | Natural English with accurate sense |
| PNEUMA | "deceived many with his false words" | Dynamic — "deceived" is more direct |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "led many astray with deceitful words." Preserves the leading-astray imagery central to Qumran polemic while being natural English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:3-4 — "Interpreter of Knowledge" vs. "Teacher who reveals true knowledge"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Interpreter of Knowledge" | Literal rendering of *doresh ha-da'at* |
| LOGOS | "Interpreter of Knowledge" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "Teacher who reveals true knowledge" | Expanded for modern comprehension |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Interpreter of Knowledge" (EMET/LOGOS). This is a technical sectarian title; PNEUMA's expansion conflates it with the Teacher of Righteousness.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:5 — "plague" vs. "pestilence" vs. "disease"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "plague" | Common rendering of *dever* |
| LOGOS | "pestilence" | More formal register |
| PNEUMA | "disease" | Accessible modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "plague" — familiar biblical term, concise, and accurate.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 1:6 — Psalm 37:10 — "shall be no more" vs. "will vanish"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the wicked-one shall be no more" | Literal *ve-ein rasha* |
| LOGOS | "the wicked shall be no more" | Standard Psalm rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the wicked will vanish" | Dynamic, vivid |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS phrasing — faithful to the Hebrew idiom and recognizable from Psalm tradition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:10 — "Congregation of the Poor" — capitalization and rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "congregation of the poor-ones" | Literal with hyphenated compound |
| LOGOS | "Congregation of the Poor" | Capitalized as community title |
| PNEUMA | "community of God's poor" | Adds "God's" for theological clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "Congregation of the Poor" — capitalized as a recognized self-designation of the Qumran community. PNEUMA's addition of "God's" is interpretive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:11 — "Belial" vs. "the Devil"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Belial" | Preserves Hebrew name of the demonic figure |
| LOGOS | "Belial" | Standard DSS scholarly term |
| PNEUMA | "the Devil" | Modern equivalent for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "Belial" (EMET/LOGOS). This is a distinctive Qumran theological term that should not be collapsed into "the Devil."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:12 — "grow fat" vs. "feast"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "grow-fat on every delicacy" | Literal Hebrew verb |
| LOGOS | "feast on every delicacy" | Natural English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "feast on every rich delight" | Expanded for impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "feast on every delicacy of the flesh" — captures the sense without EMET's jarring literalism or PNEUMA's expansion.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 1: 8**
